A Values Led School

We are a dedicated and forward-thinking school where each child’s academic achievement and personal development are important. Our motto, Celebrating Diversity, Nurturing Talent, Inspiring Achievement, supported by our values, reflects our intent as a school for all our students.
Weston Secondary School aims to inspire and develop its students and support our diverse community.

Young Carers
Supporting young carers is an important aspect of student welfare at Weston Secondary School.
A young carer is a young person who looks after someone who could not manage without their help. This could mean looking after a parent, brother or sister, or another family member living in the household with a disability, long term illness, mental health or drug and alcohol related issues. It could also mean living with the emotional impact of a sudden health event within the family, or a terminal diagnosis. When this is a parent, it can also result in responsibility or care for siblings.
As many as one in 12 students could be a young carer, and unless the school is advised about a student’s home circumstances, young carers risk first being identified by negative aspects of their behaviour or work. Some young carers worry about bullying and may be tired or worried, find it difficult to concentrate and have limited time for friendships and activities after school. If this is the case, we can help.
At Weston Secondary School, we support young carers by holding open conversations about their caring circumstances. We are developing a range of supportive interventions including a weekly lunch time drop in where they can build friendships with other young carers and receive support from staff.
Here is some useful information about young carers and the school’s commitment:
Whole School Commitment Young Carers Policy
You can identify yourself or your child as a carer by completing these forms:
Southampton Young Carers offers fantastic provision outside of school and we highly recommend getting in contact and completing a referral form – click here.
Finally, please do not hesitate to contact the school if you would like to discuss any of the above at info@westonsecondary.co.uk

Independent Learning
At Weston Secondary School we want all our students to aspire to be the best they can be. To support academic development we provide opportunities for students to learn beyond the classroom or school learning space through a series of tasks. These tasks are designed to embed learning and deepen knowledge and understanding.
To ensure we can support students with knowledge acquisition across a wide range of subjects, and provide a range of different experiences, departments utilise a range of different online platforms and paper based work . To support clarity and consistency of expectations, all homework is shared via Bromcom.
It is crucial that students engage proactively with the work set by teachers to allow them to fulfil their full potential. We strongly encourage Parents and Carers to have conversations with their children about this work to reiterate its importance. Parents and carers can view tasks set through the MyChildAtSchool (MCAS) platform.
As a school we are mindful that our students have other commitments outside of school and recognise that personal development, such as attending clubs and groups is as important as academic achievement. To support an effective balance students will receive homework in line with the expectations below.
Frequency
Key Stage 3: Years 7,8 & 9
Minimum of 30 minutes
Key Stage 4: Years 10 & 11
Minimum of 45 minutes
Rewards
As a school, we believe in praising and rewarding those who demonstrate completion of the work set. Positive points will be added via Bromcom to reflect the student’s effort or achievement. Half termly rewards are in place for students in each year group with the highest homework positives.
Homework Club
We recognise that not all our students are able to complete work at home. To support our students, we offer homework club on Mondays and Wednesdays after school until 3:50 PM. Students have access to computers and a quiet space to complete their tasks.
Useful Links
Seneca – Learn 2x Faster
Supporting at home
We recognise that supporting children at home with homework can be complex. The following link provide support and guidance for parents and carers.
Supporting learning at home | Parentkind
If you would any further help please contact your child’s tutor.
If you have any questions about work that has been set for your child please contact the class teacher in the first instance. If you have a general questions about homework please contact Mrs Bungay, Deputy Headteacher.

Subject Areas
At Weston Secondary School, we want all our students to fully engage in all aspects of school life, becoming an integral part of the school community. We want our school to be a place of welcome where students will know that their language, culture, religion and traditions are embraced, respected and celebrated.
The curriculum at Weston Secondary School has been designed to open doors to our students’ future learning and employment. We believe that character and academic performance go hand in hand if a young person is to have a successful education that provides many opportunities for their future.
Our core values; aspire, believe, achieve are at the heart of everything we do. We set high expectations of ourselves and our students to ensure that every student can achieve the very best outcomes and develop a passion for lifelong learning.
The curriculum at Weston Secondary School has been shaped to meet the needs and aspirations of every student. We offer an ambitious and knowledge-based curriculum that is carefully mapped to build and secure deep knowledge and skills across KS3 and KS4 so that students leave us well prepared and equipped to take their next steps in their education, training, employment or beyond Weston Secondary School and to develop their role as a British citizen.

pageCache.text:
Senior Leadership Team
Mr D Butterworth
Headteacher
I am incredibly proud to be Headteacher of Weston Secondary School and excited about leading our amazing school on its journey ahead. Having grown up in the local area, the community holds a special place in my heart. Therefore, I am committed to celebrating the diversity of our students, nurturing their many talents and inspiring them to achieve beyond their expectations.
In 2005 I graduated from Chichester University with a BSc (Hons) in Sports Physiotherapy. I then qualified as a teacher in 2006. I began my teaching career as a PE teacher at an outstanding school in Southampton, later becoming a Head of Year. After 6 great years I gained promotion to Assistant Headteacher at a good Hampshire school. Over 13 years of senior leadership including 5 years as a Deputy Headteacher, I successfully led the school in key areas such as pastoral support, curriculum, and teaching and learning. By far the pinnacle of my career was becoming Headteacher at Weston in 2024. I feel truly blessed and grateful that I am able lead this caring and aspirational school.
Education is the key to every child’s future; therefore, it is our responsibility to encourage our students to aspire, believe and achieve through a broad, balanced and ambitious curriculum that provides them with the platform to later thrive in further education, apprenticeships, or the workplace. I wish for our students to leave us at the end of Year 11 being kind, considerate and responsible citizens.
Aside from my role as Headteacher, I am a proud husband and father to two amazing children. I like to spend my spare time watching my daughter horse ride and coaching my son’s football team.
Mrs N Bungay
Deputy Headteacher
I am very privileged to be Deputy Headteacher at Weston Secondary School. I am passionate about working with all staff, students and parents to ensure we nurture talent, celebrate diversity and provide opportunities for excellence within our community. It is my aspiration to inspire our students to be the best version of themselves, to celebrate their achievements and to help them flourish both academically and personally.
I graduated from the University of Plymouth with a BA (Hons) in International Business and French and then went on to complete my PGCE in Modern Foreign Languages at the University of Portsmouth. In my time within the profession, I have been fortunate to have been part of 2 good secondary schools in Hampshire, most recently as Acting Deputy Headteacher and Senior Assistant Headteacher at a school in Fareham. Prior to this I spent 13 years at a school near Waterlooville, where I began my teaching career. During my time at this school, I was quickly promoted through Middle Leadership positions to Assistant Headteacher. I am proud to have been part of the journeys of these schools and to have successfully led in key areas such as Behaviour, Safeguarding, Pastoral Care, Attendance, Raising Standards and Teaching and Learning.
I am a firm believer that all students deserve the best possible education. I am very committed to ensuring Weston Secondary School is an establishment where students feel safe, supported to achieve their full potential, and encouraged to believe anything is possible.
Mr S Smith
Senior Assistant Headteacher
It is an absolute privilege to have been working at Weston Secondary School (formerly Chamberlayne College and before that Chamberlayne Park) since 2003. Serving this community has given me a huge amount of job satisfaction and unforgettable experiences. Every day I strive to provide the best I can for the students here because they absolutely deserve it. I am immensely proud to have seen so many students over the years aspire to do great things and then to know that I have played a small part in firstly, helping them believe in themselves and secondly, going on to achieve their ambitions.
I grew up in Bitterne and attended Bitterne Park School. Even at such a young age (I am still young now of course) I aspired to be a teacher. I took inspiration from the education I received and like most teachers, wished to inspire future generations in return and so my educational pathway was mapped (bad Geography joke!) out for me already. I attended Itchen College between 1997 and 1999 before studying my Geography degree at Portsmouth University until 2002. I then completed a PGCE in Secondary Education at Southampton University in 2003.
Opportunities for career progression and have a wider school impact along with my love for this community have made it an easy choice to serve Weston students for so long. After a few years as a teacher, I became a Head of Year before becoming the Key Stage 4 Progress Manager. This role developed into me becoming the school’s Raising Standards Leader regularly working with the Senior Leadership Team for many years before I joined the SLT permanently in 2022. Within my role I have a particular passion for analysing performance and progress data and then working alongside our amazing staff to improve each student’s academic outcomes so they can keep the doors open that will enable them to achieve their dreams.
Away from school I am married to an amazing primary school teacher and have two wonderful children. My daughter is football mad, and we are both Saints season ticket holders whilst my son takes great pleasure in supporting whoever they are playing against because he finds it funny. He also loves video games and visiting zoos, farms and safari parks.
Mr C Collins
Assistant Headteacher - Inclusion
I graduated from the University of Chichester in 2004 with a 2:1 BA (Hons) in Physical Education with QTS. Over the past 20 years, I’ve worked in two local schools, progressing through roles as a PE Teacher, Head of PE, and Senior Leader. Throughout my career, I’ve been driven by a strong belief that all children, regardless of their background or ability, deserve access to a first-class education.
My journey into Senior Leadership began in 2018, when I was invited to lead on Teaching and Learning. This role allowed me to help shape the school’s pedagogical vision, ensuring our students received high-quality, consistent teaching each day. I also supported staff development through meaningful CPD opportunities both within school and through external partnerships. Alongside this, I had responsibility for raising standards across the school, working closely with staff to drive improvement, monitor progress, and create a culture of high expectations and achievement.
It was during this time that I discovered my true passion: inclusion and SEND. After completing my NASENCo award, I focused on driving positive change in this area, working to create an environment where every student feels seen, supported, and empowered to succeed.
I’m incredibly excited to be joining Weston Secondary School as Assistant Headteacher (Inclusion). It’s a real privilege to become part of a school that is on such a meaningful journey of change. I’m passionate about supporting every student, championing inclusive practice, and ensuring no young person is left behind. My philosophy is simple: inclusion is not a strategy to help people fit into the systems and structures that exist; it’s about transforming those systems to better serve everyone.
Outside of education, I’m a keen sportsman. I played professional football for Southampton until the age of 20, before continuing in non-league football with clubs such as Woking, Eastleigh, and Sutton United. Sport has had a huge impact on my life, it has taught me the value of teamwork, resilience, and, above all, inclusion.
I’m also a proud family man, and weekends are usually spent on the sidelines watching my daughter and son play football, with the occasional fishing trip thrown in for good measure.
Mr Luke Wilson
Assistant Headteacher - Pastoral
Mrs Nicole Kaye
Assistant Headteacher
I graduated from the Glasgow School of Art with a BA (Hons) in Fine Art, which sparked my lifelong passion for creativity and education. My teaching career began at Southampton College, where I spent 10 years in the Creative Arts faculty, delivering art and fashion across a wide range of courses, including degree-level programs.
Since then, I have had the privilege of working in two Hampshire secondary schools rated good, where I focused on raising standards in Creative Arts and Design & Technology. I am committed to ensuring that every student has access to a dynamic, inspiring curriculum that supports them to thrive.
As part of my leadership experience, I oversee PSHE Citizenship education and Careers provision. These areas are vital in preparing students for life beyond the classroom, equipping them with the knowledge, skills, and confidence to make informed decisions about their future. I am passionate about ensuring our curriculum promotes wellbeing, resilience and respect plus provides meaningful experiences and guidance into further education, training, and employment.
Weston Secondary School is a vibrant and inclusive community where every student is encouraged to achieve their best. I am proud to be part of a team that values creativity, resilience, and ambition, and works tirelessly to provide opportunities that prepare students for life beyond school.
Outside of school, I’m a proud “swim mum” and can often be found poolside supporting my youngest daughter at swim meets. Watching her dedication and determination reminds me daily of the importance of resilience and hard work, values I strive to instil in our students at Weston Secondary School.
Mrs Tracey Harper
School Business Manager
I have been extremely fortunate to have a range of experience working as a Business Manager within the Education Sector which spans 15 years. I have worked in a BESD School, Infant and Primary Schools. My previous role was Executive Business Manager for six Primary Schools.
I was appointed as Business Manager at Weston Secondary School in September 2022, and I am very proud to see the changes that have happened across the school site during my tenure. There has been a £5.5 million investment in the building completed, along with a brand-new sports hall. We have ambitious plans to improve Weston Secondary School site further and continue to be on an exciting journey. My commitment and passion are to ensure every child receives their right to an excellent education, through quality first teaching, within buildings that are fit for purpose and stimulating resources that help them engage with the curriculum.
My role as Business Manager is to ensure the budget supports the school’s priorities and it is financially sustainable moving forward.
Mrs E Church
Designated Safeguarding Lead
I am proud to have been a member of staff at Weston Secondary School for over 18 years and am fully committed to supporting our pupils and their families to enable them to lead safe and successful lives in my role as Designated Safeguarding and Attendance Lead.
I embrace the opportunity to promote strong attendance rates and encourage safe behaviours amongst our pupils, and I feel privileged to carry out this role.
I graduated from the University of Southampton with a BSc (Hons) in Psychology, and then went on to complete a Masters Degree in Education and later achieved a Doctorate of Education with a focus on the role of support staff in schools.
In my personal life, I am a keen runner, which supports both my physical and mental wellbeing. I have two little people and take an active role in their educational journeys – promoting attendance and a strong work ethic – just as my mum did for me!

Career Guidance
Careers Education, Information, Advice & Guidance (CEIAG)
All students should leave Weston Secondary School with clear post-16 pathways and be excited about their future.
Here at Weston Secondary School, we do not expect all our students to know the career that they wish to pursue, however we do want to ensure that they have high aspirations and belief in their own abilities so that they are prepared to make informed choices about their futures.
Weston Secondary School students are encouraged from the beginning of year 7 to start thinking about their skills and qualities so that they can effectively plan for their futures.
We aim to raise aspirations and provide our students with the knowledge and experience to make informed decisions for their future choices regarding further education, apprenticeships, training or work.
We work closely with local colleges, sixth forms and universities, as well as organisations and businesses so that our students get the best possible opportunities.
The school has a dedicated Director of Careers. Please get in touch with him for further information by email: careers@westonsecondary.co.uk
Our current Careers Programme can be found below:
Careers Programme 2025-2026
In this section, you will find dedicated advice and information about how we support pupils at Weston Secondary School in making their post-16 decisions and exploring available career opportunities.

EAL
English as an additional language (EAL) is a term used by the Department for Education (DfE) to refer to a pupil whose first language is other than English. The first language is the language to which the child was exposed in early development.
Children who fit within this definition may also continue to use a language other than English at home or in their community.
While EAL pupils share many common characteristics with their native English colleagues, their learning experience differs because they learn in and through another language.
At Weston, we have a small but diverse community with over 40 languages spoken by staff and students. We also have our own EAL HUB run by Mr Maguire.
The purpose of the EAL HUB at Weston is to provide bespoke support for our EAL children by teaching them in a nurturing practical way.

The EAL HUB also works with Southampton Language Services and EMAS to provide students with additional school support. It is also a place for teachers and support staff to discuss and share ideas on how to best support EAL learners
Should you require any further information, please get in touch at: info@westonsecondary.co.uk

Extra-Curricular Clubs
At Weston Secondary School, we are committed to providing a dynamic and inclusive programme of extra-curricular clubs and activities that reflect our core values: Aspire, Believe, and Achieve. We encourage every student to Aspire to discover and pursue their passions beyond the classroom, to Believe in their potential through meaningful participation and collaboration, and to Achieve personal growth, confidence, and success in a supportive environment. Through a wide range of opportunities from creative arts to sports and cultural activities, we aim to inspire our students to become well-rounded individuals who contribute positively to our school community and beyond.
By offering a wide range of opportunities we strive to enrich the overall experience and well-being of our students, encouraging lifelong learning and meaningful connections.
Summer Clubs and Activities
Purpose of attending extra-curricular clubs
1. Personal Development
Encouraging independence and self-motivation through participation
2. Social Growth
Improving teamwork and communication through collaborative activities
3. Academic Enrichment
4. Wellbeing and Enjoyment
Encouraging physical activity and mental engagement.
5. Achievement and Recognition

Praise & Rewards
At Weston Secondary School, we are passionate about celebrating the successes of our students and our staff are very proactive in their use of rewards in and around the school. Positive recognition plays a crucial role in our school community.
Students are awarded positives in line with Aspire, Believe, Achieve.
Students work towards securing key milestones throughout the year as identified on our rewards mountains. At each stage, students can secure postcards and certificates as well as invitations to celebratory events.
Throughout the year celebration assemblies take place in school to publicly recognise students’ efforts.
To ensure our rewards are meaningful and achievable they are reviewed periodically through student voice.

Student Leadership
We recognise the importance at leadership at all levels at Weston Secondary School and are committed to providing a range of leadership opportunities for our students across all year groups.
Our student leaders are the heart of our school and work tirelessly to drive forward change and whole school improvements through our school council and student voice.
Students at Weston Secondary school can earn leadership stage badges for demonstrating their skills and abilities, in line with our ethos of Aspire, Believe, Achieve. In addition, students can apply to be part of the student leadership team.
Staff at Weston Secondary School are passionate about developing the next generation of leaders and support students in their endeavours. We encourage all our aspirant student leaders to be:
Confident
Reflective
Proactive
Resourceful
Ambitious
Flexible
Organised
Supportive
Encouraging

SEND - Special Educational Needs and Disability
At Weston Secondary School, we are proud to offer a strong, inclusive and nurturing environment for students with Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND). We believe that every child is unique and we celebrate the individual strengths, talents and qualities that each student brings to our school community. Alongside this, we work closely with students to help them overcome challenges, building their confidence, independence, and resilience so they can thrive both in school and beyond. We provide a personalised approach and are committed to ensuring that every student is known, understood and supported. By taking the time to build a detailed, individual picture of each student we can remove barriers to learning, provide tailored support both in and out of the classroom to ensure every student can achieve their full potential.
At Weston, we have high expectation and aspirations for all our students. We believe with the right support, encouragement and opportunities, all students can succeed academically, socially and personally. Our focus is not just on outcomes but developing well-rounded, confident independent individuals. We are fortunate to have a passionate and highly committed Inclusion Team who work tirelessly to support our students which includes dedicated in class support, small group interventions, 1:1 targeted support and pastoral and wellbeing provision. Together, our staff create a learning environment where students feel safe, supported and able to achieve. Further information cab be found on our SEND policy, SEND Information and accessibility plan here. Furthermore you can also access the Local Authority offer here
For any queries, please contact your child’s tutor in the first instance. Our SEND Coordinator (SENCo), Hannah Barron, can also be contacted directly at info@westonsecondary.co.uk using ‘FAO SENCo’ in the subject line. You may also reach out to the SENCo regarding any concerns or complaints related to SEND provision.

pageCache.text:
The Duke of Edinburgh Award
We are proud to offer the Duke of Edinburgh Award (DofE) at Bronze level here at Weston Secondary School, available to all students in Year 9 and above.
Award Sections
At Bronze level, the Duke of Edinburgh Award consists of four sections:
Participants must complete a 3-month programme in each of the first three sections (6 months for one section of their choice) and then a two-day expedition with an overnight camp. A training and practice expedition is carried out before the assessed expedition, usually across June and July.
Volunteering
Physical
Expedition
In-School Support
The school can provide support with completing all sections of the award, or you may wish to choose to carry out your Volunteering, Physical, or Skills sections outside of school – for example, with Scouting organisations, sports clubs or other community facilities.
Participants have recently volunteered at local early years nurseries, youth clubs, Sea Scouts, and animal shelters.
Skills such as learning a musical instrument or computer coding can be verified by staff at the school, while others such as learning to sail, circus skills, and cycle maintenance (just a few examples of recent skills undertaken by our DofE participants) can be signed off by external mentors.
The Physical section can be as simple as going for a run regularly, cycling to school, or participating in any team sport either in school or at a club outside of school.
Expedition
Our participants who complete the Bronze Award will often say the expedition, while challenging, is their favourite part of DofE.
At Bronze level, we are able to condense the training and practice parts of the expedition into one weekend, usually in June. Participants will then complete their two-day assessed expedition in July. Having hopefully completed their three other sections, successful completion of the expedition is the culmination of the bronze award, and they can be presented with their badges and certificates at the end of year assembly for their year group.
Taking part in DofE
The Duke of Edinburgh Award scheme starts in September each year, where we invite the new Year 9 cohort to sign up and begin their volunteering, physical, and skills sections. Please keep an eye out for a letter inviting your child to sign up early in the Autumn Term.
While we encourage everyone to start the programme in Year 9, students in Years 10 and 11 can participate, as long as this does not clash with exams.
If you want more information regarding the DofE scheme at Weston Secondary School, please email the DofE team. In addition, the DofE website is an excellent resource for general info: https://www.dofe.org/do/parents/.

Gateway
Our Gateway Provision is a nurturing and structured curriculum support pathway designed to meet the diverse social, emotional, and mental health (SEMH) needs of students and address any gaps in foundational skills empowering them to thrive within our mainstream school environment. We understand that each young person’s journey is unique, and our provision offers a tailored approach that bridges the gap between specialist intervention and successful reintegration into the wider school community.
At the heart of Gateway is a strong focus on equipping students with the skills, confidence, and resilience needed to succeed academically and socially. We work in close collaboration with the core subject departments to ensure that essential curriculum concepts in English, Maths, and PSHE are embedded into students’ daily experiences—both in and beyond the classroom.
Our curriculum is holistic and responsive, with a broad offer that includes:
Staffed by a committed team of experienced professionals, Gateway is a safe and inclusive environment where strong relationships and high expectations go hand in hand. We prioritise early intervention, positive behaviour support, and consistent routines, helping students to rebuild their confidence and rediscover a love of learning. Ultimately, our goal is to enable every student to transition back into the mainstream setting with the tools they need to flourish, not just academically, but socially and emotionally too.

Intent
At Weston Secondary School, we want all our students to fully engage in all aspects of school life, becoming an integral part of the school community. We want our school to be a place of welcome where students will know that their language, culture, religion and traditions are embraced, respected and celebrated.
The curriculum at Weston Secondary School has been designed to open doors to our students’ future learning and employment. We believe that character and academic performance go hand in hand if a young person is to have a successful education that provides many opportunities for their future.
Our core values; aspire, believe, achieve are at the heart of everything we do. We set high expectations of ourselves and our students to ensure that every student can achieve the very best outcomes and develop a passion for lifelong learning.
The curriculum at Weston Secondary School has been shaped to meet the needs and aspirations of every student. We offer an ambitious and knowledge-based curriculum that is carefully mapped to build and secure deep knowledge and skills across KS3 and KS4 so that students leave us well prepared and equipped to take their next steps in their education, training, employment or beyond Weston Secondary School and to develop their role as a British citizen.

Teaching and Learning
“Children need to be challenged and pushed not to the point where they give up but to the point to where they think, “WOW, look at me go. “Robert John Meehan
At Weston Secondary School (WSS) we are passionate about providing our students with the best learning experiences both inside and outside the classroom. All staff at WSS recognise the importance of education to young people and work tirelessly to ensure they have the best experience possible so they can go on to fulfil their full potential. It is our belief that there is no limit to what a young person can achieve. We are fully committed to ensuring our vales; aspire, believe and achieve come to fruition for all our students.
Through the application of a clear and consistent teaching and learning (T&L) pedagogy it is our aim to ensure all our students enjoy their learning, are provided with opportunities that enrich their lives and are able excel in their examinations.
As a HAMWIC school we always place Sam – our notional child’s – entitlement at the heart of all decisions to ensure we remain student focused. Our students are at the heart of our school community, and their needs are our priority.
We are a fully inclusive school that values the unique skills and capabilities of all students. We work collaboratively as a staff body to ensure our that teaching nurtures and challenges all students.
Pedagogy
All teachers have a responsibility to plan and deliver lessons that are personalised to the students in their class, ensuring the level of pace and challenge encourages an ethos of high aspiration. We recognise that excellent teaching fosters a culture for excellent learning.
It is our expectation that all students’ access quality first teaching every day to support academic success. The role of all teachers is to promote a culture of excellence through the provision of supportive, challenging and engaging lessons.
At WSS our pedagogy provides clarity for staff and students to maximise learning and support a reduction of cognitive load. At WSS teachers will:
Provide timely feedback to students
Student Voice
Student voice is integral to our T&L provision. At WSS students can share their views about their learning via school council. Each department also engages with student voice regularly.
Continuous Professional Development (CPD)
Senior Leaders and the HAMWIC Trust recognise the importance of providing high quality professional development for teachers. To support our teachers WSS provides a range of whole school, personalised and bespoke CPD across the academic year. At WSS Teachers are also strongly encouraged to take ownership of their own CPD to support personal and professional growth.
